questions.question: A study app requests contacts although it never uses them. What should the designer do?

options.value: Hide the permission in a menu

questions.explanation: Collect only data required for the stated purpose.

questions.question: Which improves access for students who cannot distinguish red and green?
questions.explanation: Multiple cues convey information without depending on color vision.

questions.question: Before reusing an online code library, what should a developer check?
questions.explanation: Availability online does not remove intellectual-property conditions.

questions.question: A predictive tool performs poorly for a minority group. What is the best response?

options.value: Investigate data and outcomes for that group

questions.explanation: Evaluate impacts across affected groups and address unequal errors.

questions.question: A school deploys facial recognition for attendance. What should be considered?
questions.explanation: Design decisions affect privacy, access, and people beyond the developer.

questions.question: Which practice improves accessibility for screen-reader users?
questions.explanation: Assistive technologies need a clear semantic description of controls.

questions.question: What should a program specification describe?
questions.explanation: A specification communicates requirements before implementation.

questions.question: A new feature increases energy consumption substantially. What should be evaluated?

options.value: Its benefit relative to resource use

questions.explanation: Responsible design includes environmental and resource impacts.

questions.question: What is an unintended consequence?

options.value: An effect the designers did not anticipate

questions.explanation: Systems can affect people in ways beyond the intended purpose.

questions.question: Which supports informed consent?

options.value: Explain what is collected and how it is used

questions.explanation: Users need understandable information and a meaningful choice.

questions.question: Why involve diverse users in testing?

options.value: To discover different needs and barriers

questions.explanation: Different experiences reveal assumptions that a narrow team may miss.

questions.question: Which best respects intellectual property?

options.value: Rename copied code to claim authorship
Use permitted material and give required credit

questions.explanation: Licenses and attribution apply even when material is easy to copy.

questions.question: Why document limitations of an automated recommendation?

options.value: To help users interpret results appropriately
To prove results are always right

questions.question: A design excludes users with slow internet. What is a useful response?

options.value: Reduce required bandwidth and test slower connections

questions.explanation: Access depends on device and network constraints as well as interface design.

questions.question: Who can be a stakeholder in a public software system?
questions.explanation: Impacts extend beyond the team and direct users.

questions.question: What should happen when testing reveals a harmful design assumption?

options.value: Preserve it because code is finished
Change the documentation to conceal it

questions.explanation: Testing informs iterative improvement of behavior and impacts.
